task.description:
Implement the gated design in `lib/letflow/design/iss0111-with-only-this-tenant-visible-advisory-lock-fix.md` section 3 in full -- read the whole document first, it is the exact specification (lock key, acquire/release helpers, the new `with_only_this_tenant_visible!/2` body shape wrapped in one `Repo.checkout/2`, and the required change to `restore_orphaned_guard_backup_rows!/0` to acquire the same lock). Section 3.4's table states the exact acquire/release points; section 5's open question about `Repo.checkout/2`'s return-value semantics is yours to resolve empirically (verify what `Repo.checkout/2` returns and confirm `with_only_this_tenant_visible!/2`'s existing contract -- whatever it returns today -- is preserved unchanged by the new wrapper).

This is test-file-only work (`test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs`) -- no `lib/letflow/` or migration file changes. Implement exactly what the design specifies; do not improvise beyond it. If you find the design under-specifies something, report it rather than guessing.

After implementing: run the affected tests directly (`mix test test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs`) and quote real output. This fix cannot be proven correct by a single serial run alone, since the defect only manifests under CONCURRENT invocation -- construct a targeted verification: run two `mix test` invocations against `test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs`'s ISS-0060 guard test SIMULTANEOUSLY (e.g. two background shell invocations started close together) and confirm neither corrupts the other's view of `tenant_schemas` -- report exactly what you did and what you observed. If constructing genuine concurrency is impractical in this environment, say so explicitly and explain what your single-invocation run does and does not prove, per this project's own no-speculation discipline.
acceptance_criteria: test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs implements section 3's exact specification: @guard_lock_key, acquire/release helpers, the new with_only_this_tenant_visible!/2 body wrapped in one Repo.checkout/2, and restore_orphaned_guard_backup_rows!/0 acquiring the same lock in its own Repo.checkout/2
The Repo.checkout/2 return-value question (design section 5) is resolved empirically and with_only_this_tenant_visible!/2's existing return contract is confirmed preserved
mix test test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs is actually run and real output (pass/fail counts) is quoted

A genuine concurrent-invocation verification is attempted and its real result reported, or the environment's limitation is stated explicitly with what a single-invocation run does and does not establish
No file outside test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs is modified

result.summary: Implemented design section 3 in full in test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs: @guard_lock_key literal (hashtext idiom matching lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex), acquire_guard_lock!/0 and release_guard_lock!/0 helpers, with_only_this_tenant_visible!/2's body rewrapped in one Repo.checkout/2 (acquire -> move-out -> nested try/after around fun.() with move-back -> release, outer after releases the lock), and restore_orphaned_guard_backup_rows!/0 changed to acquire/release the same lock in its own Repo.checkout/2 around its existing restore CTE. No lib/ or migration file touched. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` exits 0. `mix test test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs` (after cleaning 4 pre-existing orphaned public.iss060_tenant_schemas_guard_backup rows left over from an unrelated prior crashed run, referencing tenants no longer in public.tenants -- a pre-existing environment-state issue, not caused by this change, confirmed by re-querying the table before/after cleanup) -- real result: 10 tests, 0 failures, 'Result: 10 passed'. Design section 5's Repo.checkout/2 return-value question confirmed empirically: deps/ecto/lib/ecto/repo.ex's generated checkout/2 returns the callback's result directly with no wrapping, and the full suite pass (including the pre-existing assertions on with_only_this_tenant_visible!/2's return-based control flow) confirms the existing contract is unchanged. Concurrent-invocation verification: ran two full `mix test test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs --only line:565` OS processes simultaneously -- both actually collided, but on an unrelated pre-existing defect (System.unique_integer/1's counter restarts per-BEAM-node, so two separate `mix test` processes independently generated the identical migration version 900000001, causing a real schema_migrations collision masking any signal about the advisory lock itself; this is an adjacent gap in the test file's own version-uniqueness scheme, not something section 3 asked me to fix, and I did not touch it per the no-improvising instruction). To isolate the actual mechanism section 3 changes, I wrote a small scratch script (not committed) that runs only the acquire/sleep(2s)/release sequence via Repo.checkout/2 + pg_advisory_lock(hashtext($1)) with the exact @guard_lock_key, and ran it as two separate `mix run` OS processes started ~0.3s apart. Real observed evidence: process B's own Postgrex debug log shows `QUERY OK db=1703.8ms` for its pg_advisory_lock call -- i.e. B's acquire blocked inside Postgres itself for ~1.7s before returning, consistent with A holding the session-level lock for its full 2s sleep. This directly demonstrates cross-OS-process mutual exclusion via the advisory lock (the load-bearing property ISS-0111's fix depends on). What this does NOT prove: that two genuinely concurrent full `mix test` runs of the guard test *end-to-end* (through Ecto.Migrator.run/4) succeed cleanly -- that remains blocked by the separate unique_drop_migration_version()/System.unique_integer collision described above, which is a pre-existing gap this handoff's scope did not include fixing; flagging it as a follow-on rather than silently patching it.
issues: Pre-existing, out-of-scope: unique_drop_migration_version/0 (test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs) uses System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]), whose counter restarts per BEAM node -- two separate `mix test` OS processes can independently generate the identical migration version number, causing a real schema_migrations collision that is unrelated to ISS-0111's advisory-lock fix but blocks proving true multi-process test-suite concurrency end-to-end. Worth its own follow-up (possibly folded into ISS-0107's nested-mix-test family).

Found and cleaned up, not caused by this change: 4 stale rows in public.iss060_tenant_schemas_guard_backup referencing tenants no longer present in public.tenants (from an earlier crashed/interrupted run), which made every test in this file fail via a foreign-key violation in restore_orphaned_guard_backup_rows!/0's setup call until deleted. Confirms this project's own self-heal design assumption (a crashed invocation's owning tenant still exists) can be violated if the tenant row itself was also cleaned up around the same crash window -- noted for awareness, not fixed here (out of section 3's scope).
result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (test-only change, no tenant-data path, but flag as touching cross-invocation test-DB safety) or directly to REVIEWER per WF-03 Step 2a routing; ORCH to decide per gating rules.
